answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may bid, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated work or collusion. Splitting one attacker into a spiral of identities does not create free influence: every identity needs capital, and honest agents can challenge suspicious claims to trigger review. The attacker pays both the cost of tying up funds and the expected loss of stake, while legitimate participation remains open. In an orchard of competing services, even a shared pigment of branding cannot substitute for that collateral.
